newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian gunmen shoot dead 14 in killing spree.
newsitem.headline: Colombian gunmen shoot dead 14 in killing spree.

text.p: Suspected right-wing gunmen killed at least 14 people in Colombia, nine of them in the violence-torn northern province of Cesar, in a 24-hour shooting spree, authorities said on Saturday.

Police said the killings began shortly before dawn on Friday when three men and two women were shot to death by a gang of about 20 masked gunmen in two working class districts of Valledupar, the capital of Cesar.
Four other people, all apparently members of the same family, were killed in a house in a small town on the outskirts of Valledupar early on Saturday, police said.
Four men and one woman were gunned down in a bar late on Friday or early Saturday in the northwest banana-growing region of Uraba near Colombia's border with Panama.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for any of the killings but police sources said all were believed to be the work of right-wing paramiltary groups targeting suspected rebel sympathisers.
